security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, destructive command intent, or executable code in the skill file.

static_findings.snippet: - Collection group rules if using `collectionGroup()` queries
- Return `{ success: boolean, message: string, data?: any }`
- No `allow read, write: if true;` in rules
| No default deny rule | Add `match /{document=**} { allow: if false; }` |
| Inconsistent response format | Standardize to `{success, message, data?}` |

content.value_statement: Firebase projects can ship with weak rules, missing tests, or unsafe deployment settings. This skill guides a structured review of configuration, authentication, functions, and release readiness.
actual_capabilities: Reviews firebase.json hosting, functions, Firestore, and emulator configuration.
Checks Firestore rules for helper functions, default deny behavior, and write validation.
Reviews Cloud Functions architecture for consistent patterns and authentication handling.
Checks test coverage expectations for unit tests, emulator tests, and coverage thresholds.
Reviews production readiness items such as secrets handling, builds, tests, audits, and indexes.
Produces severity-based findings with remediation recommendations.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not deploy or modify Firebase resources.
It depends on the project files and context available to the AI assistant.
It does not replace penetration testing or a Firebase console configuration review.
Command checks may require local dependencies and explicit user permission.

use_cases.title: Pre-release Firebase review
use_cases.description: Validate rules, functions, tests, and deployment settings before a production launch.

use_cases.title: Security rules audit
use_cases.description: Check Firestore access rules for ownership checks, field validation, and default deny coverage.

use_cases.title: Architecture consistency check
use_cases.description: Review Cloud Functions organization, authentication flow, and shared patterns across a team project.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Firebase project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a visible project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Firebase project for security, configuration, tests, and production readiness. Summarize critical, important, and nice-to-have findings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Firestore rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of database access control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Firestore rules in this project. Check authentication, ownership, field validation, collection group coverage, and default deny behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check functions architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Cloud Functions implementation. Identify the architecture pattern, authentication approach, error handling, response format, and test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for production launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a production readiness audit for this Firebase application. Include configuration, rules, authentication, tests, secrets handling, build status, and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: Review this Firebase project before launch.
output: Critical: Firestore rules do not include a default deny rule.
Important: Emulator tests are missing for the main write workflows.
Nice-to-have: Document the selected functions architecture in the project README.

output_examples.input: Check our authentication and API key handling.
output: Authentication checks are present in callable functions.
API key status validation should confirm active keys before attaching user identity.
Add tests for invalid, inactive, and missing credentials.

output_examples.input: Validate production readiness for this Firebase app.
output: Build and test commands should pass in the local project environment.
Secrets should be excluded from source control and documented for deployment.
Indexes should cover complex Firestore queries before launch.

best_practices: Run the review against the same architecture pattern the project intends to use.
Review Firestore rules with representative user roles and write scenarios.
Confirm risky command checks with the user before running local project scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not mix Express, domain-grouped, and individual function patterns without a migration plan.
Do not accept broad Firestore write access without field-level validation.
Do not treat passing builds as proof that security rules are correct.

faq.question: Does this skill change my Firebase project?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and recommends fixes. Any edits require a separate user request.

faq.question: Can it review Firestore security rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks authentication, ownership, allowed field changes, collection group rules, and default deny coverage.

faq.question: Does it run Firebase deployments?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for validation before deployment, not for deploying resources.

faq.question: Can it check Cloud Functions structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews architecture pattern, exports, shared code, authentication, error handling, and response consistency.

faq.question: Should commands be run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Local commands should be confirmed with the user, especially test and build scripts from a project repository.

faq.question: Is this a full security assessment?
faq.answer: No. It is a structured Firebase code review aid and should be combined with manual testing for high-risk applications.
